examName: Designing and Implementing Cloud-Native Applications Using Microsoft Azure Cosmos DB
note: Domains and weights follow Microsoft's published skills-measured outline for DP-420, 'Skills measured as of July 21, 2026'. Two of its five domains sit at 5-10%, the smallest bands in the catalogue, so the paper carries only 4 and 5 questions in them. Always check learn.microsoft.com for the current official breakdown before your exam, as Microsoft periodically revises exam blueprints.

domains.name: Design and implement data models
subtopics: Store multiple entity types in one container and multiple related entities in one document
Denormalise data across documents and reference between documents
Identify partition key, id, and unique keys, and identify data and access patterns
Specify a default time to live on a container and design for document and schema versioning
Choose a partitioning strategy and a partition key, and plan for transactions when choosing one
Evaluate the cost of cross-partition queries and the distribution of data and throughput
Construct a synthetic partition key and design a hierarchical partition key
Choose between serverless and provisioned throughput and when to use database-level throughput
Choose a connectivity mode, implement a client singleton, and handle connection errors
Implement queries and point operations with the SDK, including transactional batch, bulk, ETags, and pagination

domains.name: Design and implement data distribution
subtopics: Choose when to distribute data across regions
Define automatic failover policies and perform manual failovers
Choose a consistency model and identify use cases for each
Evaluate the impact of consistency choices on availability, request unit cost, latency, and performance
Specify application connections to replicated data
Choose when to use multi-region writes and implement them
Implement a custom conflict resolution policy

domains.name: Integrate an Azure Cosmos DB solution
subtopics: Configure Azure Cosmos DB mirroring for Microsoft Fabric
Choose between mirroring and the Azure Cosmos DB Spark connector
Enable the analytical store on a container and query it from Azure Synapse
Implement change data capture in the analytical store
Integrate events with other applications by using Azure Functions and Event Hubs
Denormalise, enforce referential integrity, aggregate, and archive by using change feed and Functions
Implement Azure AI Search over an Azure Cosmos DB solution

domains.name: Optimize an Azure Cosmos DB solution
subtopics: Adjust indexes and calculate the cost of a query
Retrieve the request unit cost of a point operation or query
Implement the Azure Cosmos DB integrated cache
Develop an Azure Functions trigger to process a change feed
Consume a change feed from an application by using the SDK
Manage the number of change feed instances by using the change feed estimator
Implement denormalisation, referential enforcement, aggregation, and archiving with a change feed
Choose between read-heavy and write-heavy index strategies and an appropriate index type
Configure a custom indexing policy and implement a composite index
Optimise index performance

domains.name: Maintain an Azure Cosmos DB solution
subtopics: Evaluate response status codes and failure metrics
Monitor normalised RU consumption, server-side latency, and replication with Azure Monitor
Configure alerts, query resource logs, and monitor throughput and data distribution across partitions
Choose between periodic and continuous backup and configure each
Locate a restore point and restore a database or container
Choose between platform-managed and customer-managed encryption keys
Configure network-level access control and data encryption
Manage control plane and data plane access by using Azure RBAC and Microsoft Entra ID
Configure CORS settings and manage account keys by using Azure Key Vault
Choose a data movement strategy and implement a DevOps process with ARM templates and CLI
